explanation: Scan adjacent pairs, swapping whenever the required alternating inequality is reversed. The previous inequality remains satisfied after the swap, so the processed prefix stays valid. Swaps preserve every element.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: Before each step, all preceding alternating inequalities hold. Swapping a reversed pair fixes its required inequality; the moved value can only strengthen the already-fixed inequality with the previous pair. Induction establishes the full alternating order, and swaps preserve the multiset.
walkthrough: For [3,1,2], the first pair needs an increase, so swap it to [1,3,2]. The next pair already decreases. The adapter verifies 1≤3≥2 and unchanged elements.
edgeCases: Equal neighboring values satisfy both non-strict inequalities.
Empty and one-element arrays need no swaps.
The operation rearranges the supplied list.
